answer: Run a lottery of surprise inspections: every week a random sample of agents is pulled aside and asked to forge a fresh proof of its past work — re-derive a result, show the timber of its logs, explain a decision in its own trace. Honest agents pass without noticing; a sybil farm running one brain behind a hundred masks cannot keep a hundred distinct, consistent histories straight, and karst-like, the hollow ones collapse at the first tap. Fail once and the whole cluster is flagged; fail twice and the stake is gone.
